extracted.intended_audience: clinicians, clinical trialists, and medical researchers interested in randomized clinical trial design and history (particularly tuberculosis trials)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, coordinating, running and reporting randomized clinical trials (illustrated by the MRC streptomycin trial) with attention to eligibility, randomization, blinding, outcome measurement, safety monitoring and trial management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the patients participating in the trial to those aged between 15 and 30 with ‘acute progressive bilateral pulmonary tuberculosis of presumably recent origin, bacteriologically proved and unsuitable for collapse therapy’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear, specific inclusion (and implicit exclusion) criteria and ensure strict adherence to them at site level; coordinating centre should judge eligibility before enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random allocation with allocation concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each gender in each centre was allotted a numbered series of envelopes, bearing only the name of the hospital. Each envelope contained a card indicating ‘S(treptomycin)’ or ‘C(ontrol)’. The numerical order of the envelopes was based on a series of random numbers. When a patient was approved for the trial the next envelope for that centre and gender was opened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-prepared randomized lists and sealed/numbered envelopes (or equivalent methods) to conceal allocation at the point of enrollment; consider stratification (here by centre and gender) to balance important covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded outcome assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress was assessed with monthly chest X-rays, graded by three specialists who remained ignorant of (blind to) the identities of the allocation of patients to streptomycin with bed rest or bed rest alone. Monthly direct smear and culture of sputum was also reported by bacteriologists who also remained blind to the treatment group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep outcome assessors blind to treatment allocation (multiple independent assessors where appropriate) to reduce measurement bias; provide procedures for blinded laboratory and radiologic assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized co-interventions across groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the streptomycin and control group would receive the standard treatment for this type of disease—bed rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that aside from the experimental intervention, all participants receive equivalent standard care so differences can be attributed to the intervention; document and implement standard treatment protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central coordination and experienced trial management
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr Marc Daniels was appointed to coordinate the trial... supported by a highly efficient trial manager, Mrs Charlene Agnew—were the team responsible for the design, coordination, analysis and reporting of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint a central coordinating centre and experienced trial manager(s); ensure the design team includes clinicians and statisticians to manage multicentre logistics, eligibility, enrollment, data flow and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical justification and equipoise
rubrics_metrics.description: Bradford Hill proposed that it would be unethical not to assess what advantage streptomycin offered in this form of the disease compared with the current standard treatment—bed rest. This view was accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials should be ethically justified by genuine uncertainty (equipoise) about comparative benefit; weigh scarce resources (e.g., limited drug supply) and ensure fair treatment/access for control patients when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular, pre-specified outcome measurement schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress was assessed with monthly chest X-rays... Monthly direct smear and culture of sputum... Fever, weight and sedimentation rates were also recorded regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine objective outcome measures and a regular schedule for their assessment to capture short- and medium-term effects; use multiple complementary measures (clinical, radiological, microbiological).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligent data collection and case record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: My job as a clinician was to ensure strict adherence to the admission criteria, proper random allocation, organization of the standard investigations and diligent completion of the case records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rigorous site-level procedures for complete and accurate case records, adherence checks, and timely submission of forms to the coordinating centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for resolving assessor disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any difference of opinion, usually slight, was resolved by discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a prespecified method (e.g., consensus discussion or adjudication panel) for resolving disagreements among blinded assessors to maintain consistency in outcome classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled timing and confidentiality of result disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no formal indication of the results to the participating centres until the trial was completed and analysed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature disclosure of trial results to participating sites before analysis completion to prevent biasing care or subsequent assessments; manage informal communications carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety monitoring and protocol modification in response to emerging findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of bacterial resistance in the streptomycin group led the MRC to decide to discontinue treatment after only four months. Toxic effects of streptomycin can be severe... in none were they considered sufficiently severe to necessitate discontinuing treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor safety and efficacy data during the trial and be prepared to modify treatment duration or other protocol elements if new data (e.g., resistance, toxicity) indicate changed risk–benefit balance; have safety monitoring processes in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing and addressing antimicrobial resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The trials had made clear that streptomycin treatment could not be relied on to cure tuberculosis because of the development of bacterial resistance... we soon learned that a combination of streptomycin and PAS proved far more effective than either alone in treating tuberculosis, and reduced the development of resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing antimicrobial agents, include microbiological monitoring for resistance and consider trials of combination regimens to reduce resistance emergence; design trials to detect resistance patterns over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multicentre design and logistics management
rubrics_metrics.description: It was decided that there should be a series of multi-centre trials at tuberculosis units throughout the UK... As there were more patients with pulmonary tuberculosis than there were hospital or sanatorium beds to accommodate them, those allocated to bed rest alone in the trial received priority for admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan multicentre logistics (bed availability, admission priority, local policies) and account for their ethical and operational effects on recruitment and patient care; use central coordination to allocate resources fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involvement of statistical expertise in trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: Austin Bradford Hill, Professor of Medical Statistics... was one of the members of the committee... Bradford Hill had set out the principles of clinical trial design in a book based on a series of articles published in the Lancet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experienced statisticians in the design and analysis team to develop appropriate randomization, stratification, sample size considerations and analytic plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blinded/double-blind designs where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Our double blind trial proved the point [that antihistamine relieved streptomycin-induced nausea] and stimulated others to try antihistamines for sea sickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When feasible and ethical, use double-blind designs (participants and investigators blinded) for subjective outcomes or treatments affecting symptoms to reduce bias; choose blinding level according to trial aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trials as a means to inform policy and test non-drug interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized trials became a way of life, and provided much of the evidence upon which rational treatment policies came to be based... trials were also designed to assess the value of bed rest and treatment in hospital, and the preventive potential of vaccines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design trials not only for new drugs but also to evaluate care policies, delivery settings, and preventive interventions; ensure outcome measures and follow-up are appropriate to policy questions.
